_about: Wire contract consumed by Milo-Mac (github.com/leodurandfr/Milo-Mac), a SECOND API client beyond frontend/. Milo-Mac is a separate macOS app, not in this checkout, with no API versioning: if the backend drops a route or WS event listed here, Milo-Mac breaks silently at runtime. This manifest is the SOURCE OF TRUTH for that contract. Re-synced 2026-09-24 from the vendored snapshot under vendor/milo-mac/ (MiloAPIService.swift = REST, WebSocketService.swift = WS, MiloAudioState.swift = the decoder of the audio state both events and REST carry). test_milo_mac_contract.py enforces TWO things offline on every pytest run: the backend still serves every route/event here, AND this manifest matches the vendored snapshot's surface EXACTLY (so it can't silently drift from the app it protects). The non-blocking CI job check_milo_mac_freshness.py re-clones the real Milo-Mac and warns when the vendored snapshot has fallen behind upstream. Update this file + refresh vendor/milo-mac/ together, CONSCIOUSLY, in one commit when Milo-Mac evolves.

_snapshot.what_abb4902_changed: Phase 5a of the source architecture: the app reads the new audio-state wire (docs: « Développeurs : le fil », frozen 2026-09-24). WS: the four full_state carriers (system/state_changed, system/transition_start, system/transition_complete, source/state_changed) are gone, replaced by source/state, whose data IS the state; multiroom_changed is gone too — the multiroom spinner resolves on the first state where `switching` is false again with the expected `multiroom_enabled`, and routing/multiroom_error stays the failure path. REST: unchanged surface — GET /api/audio/state now decodes through MiloAudioState.swift, and the control route is sent `resume_playback` for radio. MiloAudioState.swift is vendored from this refresh on: it is byte-identical to Milo-iOS' Shared/MiloAudioState.swift (same sha256, 17bf6270…), and it is where every key the source/state invariant pins is read. Also carried: the 15 commits of Milo-Mac main since 1f708a2, among them 7f5457dc8f, which moved the eleven mutations onto sendCommand() — the extractor now reads it (backend issue #2: before, every freshness run reported eleven false GET errors).
_snapshot.why_this_key_exists: It did not, until 2026-09-20 — and that is exactly how the snapshot went six routes stale. The manifest recorded WHAT Milo-Mac consumes and never WHICH VERSION of Milo-Mac it was read from, so `manifest == snapshot` stayed green while both described an app four music-library routes out of date. The iOS manifest already carried this key and its lesson: a snapshot left stale makes the equality true trivially and the contract decorative. Bump it in the same commit as the .swift files, always.
_snapshot.what_1f708a2_added: NINE routes, all gained, none lost — six the extractor could see and three it could not: GET /api/music-library/{search,albums,artist/{},album/{}} plus the two spellings of POST /api/audio/control. The other three — GET /api/music-library/cover/{}, /api/radio/favicon and /api/radio/images/{} — are built with URLComponents or matched with hasPrefix rather than passed to send()/fetchJSON(), so the one-shape extractor reported a surface missing them and the freshness job could not have flagged them however often it ran. Found only by reading the refreshed snapshot line by line. extract_rest now reads every /api/ literal on a line of code, which is the check_milo_ios_freshness.py::unvendored_surface lesson arriving on the Mac side. Milo-Mac grew an in-app music-library browser (4808d69, 1f708a2, 2026-09-13) and the manifest was not touched. Six routes the backend was free to delete believing nobody called them — which is the whole hazard this file exists for, arrived on the Mac side after the same thing had just been caught on the iOS side.
_snapshot.the_job_caught_it_and_nobody_read_it: check_milo_mac_freshness.py did its whole job. It ran, it detected the drift, and on 2026-09-15 it opened issue #1, 'Milo-Mac contract drift: refresh the vendored snapshot', which then sat open for five days while the six routes stayed unprotected. So the failure here is NOT a missing signal and the remedy is not more automation: the job is deliberately non-blocking (it prints ::error:: annotations and still exits 0) because a scheduled clone of a third-party repo must never be able to block a merge, and that call stands. What the episode measures is the human half — an annotation and an issue are only worth what someone does with them. Worth knowing before adding a louder alarm: the alarm rang.
_snapshot.confirmed_by_the_app_author: The six routes, their call chains, the decoded response fields, the one-route-two-spellings question and the absence of WS drift were all confirmed against the source by Milo-Mac's author before anything here was edited, then re-verified against a fresh clone at this hash. Build checked on this exact commit (Debug, macOS, Xcode 27.0): BUILD SUCCEEDED. Release and Milo MacTests were NOT run.

rest.note: Body {volume_db}. The MAC travels WITHOUT colons in the path (dca6327ed343) while every response carries them — Milo-Mac strips them in macURL(_:). The backend answers 400 outside the configured limits instead of clamping, so Milo-Mac clamps on its cached limits first.
Body {delta_db} — a zone-wide DELTA the backend applies atomically, emitting a single volume_changed. Milo-Mac deliberately does not loop per-client PATCHes here.

Zone membership comes from here (Client.zone_id / Zone.client_ids); Milo-Mac never reconstructs it from equalizer groups the way frontend/ does. Decoded by MultiroomSnapshot(json:) in MultiroomModels.swift, which is NOT part of the vendored pair.
Calls the {target} route with the literal target 'local'. The backend route is templated /api/equalizer/target/{target}/enabled.
Single bulk call that replaced the per-category /api/settings/{volume-limits,volume-steps,dock-apps} GET routes. Reads volume_limits.{min_db,max_db} and dock_apps.enabled_apps from the response.

Called with ?query= from a 300 ms-debounced search field. NO `data` envelope — three lists at the ROOT: artists[], albums[], songs[]. Each element is dropped SILENTLY when it has no String `id` (compactMap over failable inits), so a renamed id does not error, it empties the list. Read per element: artists[].{id,name,albumCount,coverArt|artistImageUrl}, albums[].{id,name|title,artist,coverArt}, songs[].{id,title,artist,coverArt}.

The showcase list behind the Music Library panel. Called with ?type=&size=; `size` is MiloStore.musicLibraryShowcaseSize. TWO calls in series, not one: type=recent first, then type=newest ONLY if the first list comes back empty. Those two are the sole `type` values Milo-Mac ever sends — not random/frequent/starred, whatever its own comment suggests. Root key `albums[]`, same album shape as /search.

Subsonic nesting, and the key is SINGULAR: reads `artist.album[]`, never `artist.albums[]`. A missing `artist` node degrades to {} and yields an empty list rather than an error, so a renamed envelope shows up as an artist with no albums. Nothing else under `artist` is read — not name, not id, not coverArt: Milo-Mac already holds them from /search.

Reads `album.song[]` — singular again. The album_id may be a synthetic `mdisc:…`. TWO call profiles: one fetch to open an album page, and a PARALLEL FAN-OUT (withTaskGroup, one request per album) when a whole artist is played — a 20-album artist means 20 concurrent requests on this route. Individual failures are swallowed (`try?`) and the album is skipped, so a partial outage here is an incomplete queue with no error anywhere.

ONE backend route, TWO spellings in the Swift — see the music_library entry below; both are listed because the manifest tracks what the client DECLARES and the snapshot produces both shapes. Body {command, data}: the command names the state's `controls` lists (pause | resume | next | prev, and resume_playback for radio), param-less, with `data` an explicitly EMPTY object rather than absent. Since 7f5457dc8f every mutation goes through sendCommand(), which reads the body's `status` and treats anything but 'success' as a failure — the asymmetry this note used to record with POST /api/audio/source/{source} is gone.

The SAME route as the entry above, with `source` frozen to the literal `music_library`; the canonical spelling is /api/audio/control/{source}. Two entries because the extractor reads two literals and manifest == snapshot is a plain equality — NOT because there are two routes. They even converge at runtime: when the library is the active source and its `controls` allow the command, sendPlaybackCommand interpolates to this very URL. What separates them is the BODY, not the path: {command: 'play_context', data: {tracks: [...], start_index: Int, shuffle: false}} — shuffle is always false, Milo-Mac exposes no shuffle. `tracks` carries MusicLibrarySong.raw VERBATIM, the whole song dict as the backend served it: a ROUND-TRIP CONTRACT, not a projection. Dropping or renaming a song field Milo-Mac never reads would still break playback, which is why the four fields named in /search are not the whole dependency.

Called with ?favorites_only=true (query string is not part of the path contract). Decodes stations[].{id, name, favicon} — `favicon` is NEW in this refresh and is the station logo: empty or absent for many favorites, otherwise either a Pi-hosted path (/api/radio/images/…, used as-is) or an external URL sent through /api/radio/favicon. Milo-iOS pins the same route for its widget artwork priming, and reads none of these fields.

Cover proxy behind the whole library browser — every album, artist and song row resolves its artwork here. NOT a `send`/`fetchJSON` call: the URL is built with URLComponents and handed to an image load, so the one-shape extractor never saw it and this manifest could not list it. Deleting the route left every test green and blanked the browser. Found by reading, 2026-09-20; extract_rest now reads any /api/ literal for exactly this reason.

Proxy for an EXTERNAL station logo, called with ?url=. Same URLComponents shape, same invisibility. Milo-Mac reproduces the frontend's rule (utils/faviconUrl.js): a favicon already hosted by the Pi is used as-is, anything else goes through this proxy, which spoofs headers.

The other half of that rule, and the odd one out: Milo-Mac never BUILDS this path, it recognises it with hasPrefix on a `favicon` the backend itself served, then uses the string unchanged. The dependency is on the PREFIX staying `/api/radio/images/` — move the images elsewhere and the branch sends every local logo through the external proxy instead. A literal ending in `/` is therefore read as a prefix with a variable tail rather than a whole route, or a three-segment entry could never match the four-segment route FastAPI serves.

ws._about: Each (category, type) below MUST have at least one backend emission site: a typed WsEvent subclass (core/models/ws_events.py) referenced outside its defining module. payload_invariants are STATICALLY VERIFIED against those typed models by test_milo_mac_contract.py (test_invariant_* + test_all_payload_invariants_are_verified) — adding/changing an invariant here requires the matching test.

events.note: `data` IS the audio state (the same object GET /api/audio/state returns), decoded by MiloAudioState.decode; a state it cannot decode is logged and ignored. Pinned by the source/state payload invariant below.
Emitted as a typed VolumeLimitsChanged event through api/settings.py::_handle_setting_update.

source/state.note: Every key the decoder reads, dotted; checked against the backend's typed AudioState (core/models/audio_wire.py) AND against the vendored decoder, so neither side can drop one alone. `source`, `switching`, `service`, `controls`, the two flags, and inside a session `id`, `phase`, `senders` are decoded as REQUIRED: a missing one fails the whole state. `service` and `session.phase` are frozen enums — an unknown value fails the decode on purpose — so their values are pinned both ways. `details` is decoded leniently (try?): only the radio station and track and the library's track_id are read; `availability` is not decoded.

volume_changed.fallback: data.volume_db (Double or Int) when state is absent
volume_changed.multiroom_note: state.clients and state.zones are the ONLY real-time feed for the per-client and per-zone volumes in Milo-Mac's multiroom submenu — no other event carries them. Their contents are decoded by MultiroomVolume(state:) in MultiroomModels.swift, outside the vendored pair, so only the two keys are pinned here.
volume_changed.step_note: step_mobile_db is NO LONGER consumed — Milo-Mac's keyboard step is a local setting (GlobalHotkeyManager.volumeDeltaDb). Do not re-couple to it.

routing/multiroom_error.note: presence only; no payload field is read

multiroom/client_state_changed.note: PRESENCE ONLY — no payload field is read, since 9727a28. Both registry events now collapse to ONE signal in WebSocketService.parseMessage, `.multiroomStructureChanged`, and the store answers it by re-fetching GET /api/multiroom/state rather than applying the wire diff. The event says only THAT something moved. This entry used to pin `mac_id` and `client`, and the note explained how Milo-Mac read a null `client` — a description of code that had already been deleted. It passed the whole time because the invariant is verified against the BACKEND model, which still carries both fields; nothing ever asked the client. Same defect as the iOS `dock_apps.enabled_apps` entry, found the same way: by reading the app.

multiroom/zone_changed.note: PRESENCE ONLY — same collapse as client_state_changed above, same commit. Worth recording what this removed, because the old entry documented a REAL backend trap and it must not read as still-open: Milo-Mac used to derive member-removed from `zone == nil && mac_id != nil`, which MultiroomZoneChanged's own docstring calls wrong (a `deleted` action carries the zone dict too, so zone-presence says nothing about what happened). Milo-Mac no longer reads any of it, so the trap can no longer bite THIS client — but the discriminator is still misleading for anyone who does branch on it, and the fix would still belong in the consumer, never in a backend shim.

consumer_side_only_NOT_enforced.reason: Keepalive; Milo-Mac explicitly ignores it (its tuple switch has no arm for it). Emitted by the WS ping loop, not by broadcast_event(). NOT enforced.
